newsitem.title: INDIA: India soy trade sees early end to moisture problem.
newsitem.headline: India soy trade sees early end to moisture problem.

text.p: Indian exporters will soon be able to ship consignments of soy meal that have been held at ports because of their high moisture content, industry officials and traders said on Tuesday.

"(Out of) around 100,000 tonnes (of soy meal) which was received for shipment at various ports, only 10,000-12,000 tonnes of consignments were held back because of reports of high moisture content," Davish Jain, chairman of the Soybean Processors Association of India, said in a statement.
Those cargoes would also be fit for shipment in a few days as they dried out, Jain added.
Heavy rains during the last two weeks of November damaged part of the soybean crop and disrupted harvesting.
"Processing (of the soybean crop) is going on in full swing," Jain told Reuters.
Jain said Indian exporters had signed contracts to export more than one million tonnes of soy meal in 1996/97 (Nov-Oct).
Traders put the total at nearly 1.4 million tonnes.
Indian soymeal was currently quoted at $273 per tonne F.A.S, against $276-277 last week and around $210 a year ago, they said.
Soybeans were quoted at 10,100-10,400 rupees per tonne compared with 8,100-8,400 a year ago in the markets of central India, the hub of India's soy processing industry.
